messages:
deploy-bot: Starting config-only rollout: routing-policy=v2, default-timeout=3s -> 2s, tenant-batching.default_window=12ms. Canary: 2 hosts in eu-west. /deploy config-only --canary

alice_dev: quick summary? change window? release notes?

claire_pm: change window is 14:00-15:00 UTC. This is to reduce p99 latency for short-chat flows and tighten batching for smaller requests. Release note draft: 'Tweak routing scores and reduce per-request timeout to improve tail latency; enable tighter tiny-batch window for low-token requests.'

ben_oncall: tagging perf and errors channels. What metrics to watch for rollback?

alice_dev: watch p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate (5xx), queue-length on kvcache, and tenant-specific 429s. Also token throughput drop for embeddings.

ben_oncall: noted. I'll watch: \n- logs: service/router (error-rate)\n- infra: autoscaler triggers\n- obs: rolling-p99, request_5xx_rate

deploy-bot: Canary deployment status: step=applied, canary_hosts=2/2, health=passing. No immediate failures reported.

alice_dev: plan: let canary run for 10m, then ramp to 15% traffic for 30m with routing-weight smoothing (0.1 -> 0.15). If p99 increases >10% or 5xx >0.2% above baseline, revert.

claire_pm: also a tenant pin request: fintech-tenant needs to stay on routing-policy=v1 for compliance. Can we pin them?

alice_dev: yes, add a tenant-exclude rule before full rollout: routing-policy: default->v2, override fintech-tenant->v1. I'll push rule now. Command: 
```
/rules create --scope=tenant --tenant=fintech-tenant --policy=routing:v1 --note="preflight pin for compliance"
```

deploy-bot: Rule created: id=rule_8342, scope=tenant, tenant=fintech-tenant, policy=routing:v1

sally_sre: heads-up: if routing-weight smoothing triggers capacity shift we may see transient CPU climb on model-hosts. I'll keep infra autoscale on aggressive for next 45m.

ben_oncall: canary -> 10m elapsed. p50/p95 stable, p99 up 3%, 5xx flat. No queue growth. Proceeding to 15% ramp.

deploy-bot: Traffic ramp: 0.02 -> 0.15 over 5m. Observability hooks enabled.

alice_dev: rolling logs show tiny-batch window dropped from 25ms to ~12ms as expected. Throughput per-host slightly up (3%).

ben_oncall: 12m into 15% ramp: p99 spike observed for short-chat flow (trace ids: 7f4a, 7f4b). 5xx for router up to 0.35% (baseline 0.1%). I'm marking this as a potential rollback condition.

claire_pm: any pattern? tenant-scoped?

ben_oncall: errors concentrated on a subset of hosts routing to model_pool_a, not fintech-tenant. Could be kernel selection mismatch after routing-policy change.

alice_dev: okay, immediate mitigations: 1) scale down routing-weight to 8% for 5m, 2) enable fallback to routing:v1 for hosts showing >0.2% 5xx. I can apply a soft rollback for affected hosts only.

deploy-bot: Applying routing-weight adjustment: 0.15 -> 0.08. Applying host-specific fallback for hosts [host-1203, host-1204].

ben_oncall: after soft rollback: 5xx dropped to 0.12%, p99 trending back toward baseline. Good.

claire_pm: we should record this as a post-rollout action item: investigate kernel selection & model variant mapping for model_pool_a. Add to sprint backlog.

alice_dev: agreed. Also will add a small guard in rollout config: if host error spike occurs, auto-decrease weight and pin host to previous routing policy. Proposed new config snippet: 
```
rollout.guard: {
  error_threshold: 0.2,\n  weight_decrease_pct: 50,\n  host_fallback: true
}
```

sally_sre: SGTM. Also let's add an alert to paging if 5xx > 0.5% cluster-wide for 10m.

deploy-bot: Final status: rollout paused at 8% traffic. Canary hosts healthy. Tenant fintech-tenant remains pinned to routing:v1. Action items logged: #PR-4823 (guard change), #INC-981 (investigate model_pool_a).

alice_dev: I'll update release notes with the observed soft-fallback behavior and the guard addition. Planning follow-up patch early next week.

ben_oncall: thanks all. I'll keep an eye for 30m then either resume ramp or trigger full rollback if regressions return. :thumbsup:
